definition: In this source, transcription means the gene-expression process carried out with the help of general transcription factors and RNA Polymerase II. It refers to cellular activity that can be reduced or altered, rather than to a psychological assessment or counselling technique.

reasons: The packet supports transcription in a molecular biology/gene-expression context, not the supplied field of cognition; the field is not defensible here.
The definition adds specific mechanistic detail about general transcription factors and RNA polymerase II that is not directly defined in the packet.
The contrast with a psychological assessment or counselling technique is unsupported and out of scope for the source packet.

The packet does not define “transcription” as a gene-expression process carried out with general transcription factors and RNA Polymerase II; it only mentions TFIIA (a general transcription factor), TBP, TFIIB, and RNA polymerase II in the context of suppressing an ORC mutation phenotype.
The claim that transcription “refers to cellular activity that can be reduced or altered, rather than to a psychological assessment or counselling technique” is not supported anywhere in the packet.
